evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig; intradermal induction with Freund's complete adjuvant; topical induction; challenge at 5% LAE concentration; observation at 24 and 48 h
evidence.support_text: In dermal sensitization studies in guinea pigs, LAE was tested by intradermal injection with Freund's complete adjuvant, followed by topical induction and challenge with 5% LAE. No skin reactions were observed at the challenge sites, and the study concluded that LAE was not a skin sensitizer under the test conditions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig; intradermal induction with Freund's complete adjuvant; topical induction; challenge at 50% and 25% v/v Mirenat-N; observation at 24 and 48 h
evidence.support_text: In dermal sensitization studies in guinea pigs, Mirenat-N was tested by intradermal injection with Freund's complete adjuvant, followed by topical induction and challenge with 50% and 25% v/v Mirenat-N. No skin reactions were noted at challenge sites with either concentration or vehicle control, and the study concluded that Mirenat-N was not a skin sensitizer under the test conditions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig; topical application of liquid HFC 134a
evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test, application of liquid HFC 134a to the skin produced no signs of inducing skin sensitization, as reported by Mercier (1989, 1990a, 1990b).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs; maximization method (OECD guideline)
evidence.support_text: Skin-sensitizing properties of beryllium metal were investigated in guinea pigs (maximization method). Beryllium metal was found not to be a skin sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction by intradermal injection of TEG followed after 7 days by an epicutaneous application; after a 14 day rest period epicutaneous challenge doses applied for 24 h and site inspected for signs of irritation at 24 and 48 h after removal of the challenge patch. Challenge was with undiluted TEG.
evidence.support_text: The potential for TEG to produce an immune-mediated cutaneous hypersensitivity reaction was investigated in guinea pigs by a maximization procedure. There were no reactions indicating skin sensitization with undiluted TEG.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: intradermal injection of 1% test substance; topical application of 100% under occlusion for 48h. Challenge: topical application of 25% under occlusion for 24h. Species: guinea pig.
evidence.support_text: Trioctanoin was evaluated for skin sensitization using the Magnusson and Kligman guinea pig maximization test with induction concentrations of 1% (intradermal) and 100% (topical occlusion) and challenge at 25%. Two guinea pigs showed a slight response during the first challenge, but no reactions were noted during the second challenge. Trioctanoin was classified as a non-sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intradermal induction phase followed by topical induction phase and challenge phase; extracts prepared in 0.9% sodium chloride (SC) and cotton seed oil (CSO); scoring at 24 h and 48 h after patch removal on a 0–3 scale; 10 test animals per extract; 5 vehicle control animals per solvent.
evidence.support_text: PVA embolic microspheres (colorless and blue) were evaluated for skin sensitization by the maximization test in 30 adult albino guinea pigs. The test used extracts in saline (SC) and cotton seed oil (CSO) with intradermal induction, topical induction, and challenge phases. The maximization test disclosed no irritation to skin or tissues, indicating a negative skin sensitization result. No animal showed a score ≥1 required for a positive sensitization call under the protocol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: SC extract, guinea pig maximization test, 24 h and 48 h after challenge phase
evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test, at 24 h and 48 h after the challenge phase, no visible cutaneous reaction was observed in all skin sites of animals in the test sample group for SC extract of colorless microspheres (Table 1). This result indicates that the SC extract of colorless microspheres was not irritating to skin and not a sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Sensitized and challenged with captopril; 7 guinea pigs; observed for 24 h; vehicle control group had 0/8 sensitization.
evidence.support_text: When challenged with CP, four out of the total seven guinea pigs showed an erythematous reaction (reddening of the skin) which persisted for 24 hr, while the rest showed mild redness on the challenged area. This reaction to CP was similar to the positive control group that had been sensitized and challenged with penicillin G, a known skin sensitizer. The control group (sensitized and challenged with the vehicle only) showed a sensitization rate of 0/8.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Test article extract (SC extract of PAN A2) was administered to guinea pigs; challenge phase dermal observations graded per Magnusson and Kligman scale.
evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test, the test article extracts (SC extract of PAN A2) showed no evidence of causing delayed dermal contact sensitization. Dermal observations yielded a grading of zero under the conditions of this study, indicating no sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: undiluted, guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In guinea pig maximization tests, cetearyl nonanoate (10% in sesame oil) and undiluted neopentyl glycol diisononanoate were nonsensitizers; results for 50% cetearyl nonanoate in sesame oil and undiluted neopentyl glycol diisononanoate (for induction) were negative in preliminary skin irritation tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig; intradermal induction and topical challenge; vehicle for topical challenge: pet.; small group of test animals
evidence.support_text: The GMT results with N-6 did not reveal a greater proportion of animals responding at higher or lower intradermal induction concentrations nor did more of the exposed animals react to topical challenge than the GMT-induced animals with no N-6 exposure. It is concluded that N-6 has not been shown to be a cutaneous sensitizer for the guinea pig in this small group of test animals and it probably has a low sensitization potential for this animal.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 24 h occluded patch challenge at the maximum non-irritant concentration; Cavia porcellus
evidence.support_text: In the GPMT, 2 of the 20 guinea pigs sensitized with DCNB displayed clear skin reactions (grade 1 erythema, but no oedema) following 24 h occluded patch challenge at the maximum non-irritant concentration. None of the 10 control animals gave any skin reaction. On the basis of the Magnusson and Kligman classification, DCNB would be regarded as a mild skin sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Albino Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs were given 6 intradermal injections of 2.0% hydroquinone in 0.9% saline in the shoulder region to induce sensitization. After 6–8 days, a 48-hour occlusive patch of 1.0% hydroquinone in an acetone–polyethylene glycol 400 vehicle was placed over the injection site. The challenge was a 24-hour occlusive patch of 0.5% hydroquinone (maximum nonirritating concentration) on the flank. Responses assessed at 14 and/or 48 hours after challenge.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig maximization test, induction with 2% hydroquinone injected intradermally, followed by challenge with 0.5% hydroquinone, showed extreme sensitization. Hydroquinone was classified as an extreme sensitizer. In the detailed protocol, 100% of the animals had a positive response after 14 and/or 48 hours after challenge with 0.5% hydroquinone.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig maximization test per ISO 10993-10:2010; Fe3O4@Agar/HA extract solution; challenge skin sites observed at 24 and 48 h after dressing removal.
evidence.support_text: Young adult albino guinea pigs were used to assess the skin sensitization potential of the Fe3O4@Agar/HA extract solution through the guinea pig maximization test (GPMT). The clinical manifestations of the guinea pigs treated with the test samples and the control samples were all normal. At 24 and 48 h after the removal of the dressings, no visible changes were observed at the challenge skin sites, suggesting that Fe3O4@Agar/HA has no skin sensitization potential.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Hartley guinea pigs (n=35); specific extracts prepared from the material under test
evidence.support_text: The nano-Cu/LDPE IUD was tested for skin sensitization using the guinea pig maximization test (GPMT) in Hartley guinea pigs (n=35). No skin sensitization was identified in any animals treated with specific extracts prepared from the material.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction with Nonoxynol-6 at 1.7, 3, 9, 27 g% (w/w) in propylene glycol via intradermal injection and occlusive patch; challenge with 2.7% Nonoxynol-6 in petrolatum; guinea pigs (Hartley-Dalkin strain); scoring at 48 h.
evidence.support_text: Nonoxynol-6 was evaluated for skin sensitization using the guinea pig maximization test. Induction used concentrations of 1.7, 3, 9, and 27 g% (w/w) in propylene glycol with intradermal injections and an occlusive patch. Challenge with 2.7% Nonoxynol-6 in petrolatum yielded incidences of 2/5, 0/5, 1/4, and 2/5 in the respective dose groups, and 5/40 in controls. The proportion of reactions was not significantly different from controls, leading to the conclusion that Nonoxynol-6 did not induce sensitization in guinea pigs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 1% chlorphenesin in distilled water, intradermal injection and 48-h occlusive patch; challenge: 0.5% or 1% chlorphenesin in distilled water, 24-h occlusive patch; evaluation at 24 and 48 h after patch removal; 30 female albino Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs.
evidence.support_text: The skin sensitization potential of chlorphenesin was evaluated in a modified guinea pig maximization test using 30 female albino Dunkin-Hartley guinea pigs. Induction involved intradermal injection of 1% chlorphenesin and a 48-hour occlusive patch with 1% chlorphenesin; challenge was with 0.5% or 1% chlorphenesin under occlusive patch for 24 hours. Reactions were scored at 24 and 48 hours after patch removal. Chlorphenesin did not induce sensitization in guinea pigs at a concentration of 1%, followed by challenge with 0.5% or 1.0%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: intradermal injection of 20% Glyceryl Laurate emulsion in shoulder region; boost with occlusive patch over injection site at 7 days; challenge: occlusive patch on flank with 10% dilution of test substance at 14 days; 10 test guinea pigs, 4 controls treated only at challenge.
evidence.support_text: Kabara (1984) studied skin sensitization of a 20% Glyceryl Laurate emulsion via GPMT. Positive challenge reactions were observed in two out of ten test animals challenged with a 10% dilution of the test substance, while controls showed no reactions at that dilution.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intradermal injection on day 0 with FCA, vehicle, and test material extracts, followed by topical patch exposure on day 7 for 48 h; challenge patch on day 21 for 24 h; skin reaction grading at 24 and 48 h after challenge.
evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test, the thin film test material extracts (FLG-C and NR latex/FLG-C-NR latex) were evaluated. No skin sensitization reactions were observed in either the control or test sites of all animals, yielding a negative result for this assay.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs (Cavia porcellus) sensitized with 5% PPDA; challenge concentration of PPDA was 1% or 3%; microscopic observations on scale 0-3; Student's t-test.
evidence.support_text: Skin reaction sites from PPDA-sensitized guinea pigs showed elevated eosinophil infiltration (1.5 ± 0.3) compared to controls (0) on a 0–3 scale, and the authors state all three indices evaluated were significantly elevated.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs (Cavia porcellus) sensitized with 5% PPDA; challenge concentration of PPDA was 1% or 3%; microscopic observations on scale 0-3; Student's t-test.
evidence.support_text: Skin reaction sites from PPDA-sensitized guinea pigs showed significantly elevated acanthosis (1.8 ± 0.2) compared to controls (0.8 ± 0.3) on a 0–3 scale, consistent with a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs (Cavia porcellus) sensitized with 5% PPDA; challenge concentration of PPDA was 1% or 3%; microscopic observations on scale 0-3; Student's t-test.
evidence.support_text: Skin reaction sites from PPDA-sensitized guinea pigs showed significantly elevated mononucleocyte infiltration (1.8 ± 0.2) compared to controls (0.3 ± 0.2) on a 0–3 scale, indicative of delayed-type hypersensitivity.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: intradermal injection of 5% tox-batch and epidermal exposure to 50% tox-batch in water; challenge: 50%, 25%, and 10% tox-batch; species: albino guinea pig; assessment at 24 and 48 hr after challenge.
evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman), the tox-batch was tested for contact hypersensitivity. Induction: intradermal injection of 5% and epidermal exposure of 50% tox-batch in water; challenge: 50%, 25%, and 10% tox-batch. Positive reactions (erythema/swelling) were observed at all challenge concentrations at 24 and 48 hr, with a 100% sensitization rate. The tox-batch was classified as a strong sensitizer (Magnusson and Kligman, 1969).

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig maximization test (Magnusson and Kligman)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Standard guinea pig maximization test according to Magnusson and Kligman; DNCB used as positive control.
evidence.support_text: The well known skin sensitizer DNCB (positive control) caused skin sensitization in ten of ten animals (Table 2), indicating adequate sensitivity of the test animals.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Concentrated liquid l-lysine (50%), guinea pig, OECD Guideline 406, Guinea pig maximisation test
evidence.support_text: A skin sensitisation study with concentrated liquid l-lysine (50%) in guinea pigs (OECD Guideline 406, Guinea pig maximisation test) reported no dermal reactions at 24 or 48 hours post-challenge, and the test item was consequently considered to have no sensitising properties.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs, 99.5% pure l-lysine HCl, observations at 24 and 48 h post-challenge, in accordance with OECD Guideline 406.
evidence.support_text: The skin sensitisation potential of the l‐lysine HCl (99.5%) was studied in guinea pigs in accordance with OECD Guideline 406 (Guinea pig maximisation test). No dermal reactions were observed at the 24‐ or 48‐h post‐challenge. Consequently, the test item has no sensitising properties.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig maximization test (sensitisation test per ISO10993-10)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs, Freund's Complete Adjuvant, sodium lauryl sulphate stimulation; mean score 0.2
evidence.support_text: In the sensitisation test, guinea pigs were tested using Freund’s Complete Adjuvant and sodium lauryl sulphate. With a mean score of 0.2 (‘negligible (0–0.4)’, according to the ISO skin irritation index), these low-grade reactions do not alter the conclusion that the PMMA, primer-coated PMMA and TiO₂-coated PMMA do not cause significant skin irritation.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig maximization test and modified Draize test
evidence.experimental_conditions: 3.0% active CAPB in albino guinea pigs, topical administration
evidence.support_text: Microscopic changes in the treated skin of albino guinea pigs indicated slight delayed-type contact sensitization by a 3.0% active CAPB solution in a maximization test and modified Draize test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, open cutaneous test, details limited
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig open cutaneous test with γ-undecalactone, no skin reactions were reported (Klecak, 1985).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intracutaneous and dermal challenge in guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: In the optimization test conducted in guinea pigs, no evidence of a sensitizing potential of Gd-EOB-DTPA (gadoxetic acid) was found after the first intracutaneous and the second dermal challenge.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig passive transfer skin sensitization test
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs were made tuberculin-sensitive, then received peritoneal exudate from donors sensitized with picryl-chloride conjugated to guinea pig red cell stromata; challenge: topical application of picryl-chloride solution in oil.
evidence.support_text: Guinea pigs previously made tuberculin-sensitive were sensitized using conjugates of picryl-chloride with guinea pig red cell stromata. Intraperitoneal injection of peritoneal exudate from these animals into normal guinea pigs resulted in passive sensitization of the skin, manifested by a positive reaction to topical application of picryl-chloride solution in oil.

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, sensitized with 250 µg PDC 2 weeks prior, patch test with 3.13 µg PDC
evidence.support_text: Two weeks after sensitization with 250 µg of PDC, 55% of sensitized guinea pigs reacted to a patch test with 3.13 µg PDC, indicating an allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, sensitized with 250 µg PDC 2 weeks prior, patch test with 6.25 µg PDC
evidence.support_text: Two weeks after sensitization with 250 µg of PDC, 92% of sensitized guinea pigs reacted to a patch test with 6.25 µg PDC, indicating an allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig patch test following exclusive airway exposure
evidence.experimental_conditions: Intranasal application of 0.6, 1.2, or 1.8% TDI; subsequent patch challenge with TDI
evidence.support_text: Another group received intranasal (in.) application of 0.6, 1.2, or 1.8% TDI. Ninety-two percent (11/12) of in.-dosed animals exhibited skin sensitivity upon patch challenge with TDI. None of 14 control animals gave a positive reaction.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig patch test following exclusive airway exposure
evidence.experimental_conditions: Intratracheal administration of 50 µl of 0.6% TDI; subsequent patch challenge with TDI
evidence.support_text: A group of guinea pigs was administered 50 µl of 0.6% TDI intratracheally (it.). Eighty percent (4/5) of the it.-dosed animals exhibited skin sensitivity upon patch challenge with TDI. None of 14 control animals gave a positive reaction.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 15% in PEG 300, topical, following intradermal FCA/saline (1:1) injections; challenge: 0.5%, 1%, 3%, 5% in PEG 300; irradiation with 10 J/cm² UVA and 1.8 J/cm² UVB; Himalayan spotted guinea pigs.
evidence.support_text: In a photoallergy study, 15% 2-cyclohexyl-1,6-heptadien-3-one in PEG 300 was applied topically to guinea pigs following intradermal FCA/saline injections and irradiation with UVA and UVB. Challenge doses of 0.5% to 5% were applied and irradiated similarly. The compound did not cause any photosensitization reactions, resulting in a negative outcome.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig repeated application contact sensitivity test
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, repeated topical application of difluprednate ointment twice weekly for a total of 8 applications, observation of skin allergic reaction
evidence.support_text: Repeated topical application of difluprednate ointment to guinea pigs (twice weekly, total 8 applications) did not induce a skin allergic reaction; the response was negative.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig repeated insult patch test
evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% solution in 9:1 dipropylene glycol methyl ether:Tween 80; 0.1 ml topical application 4 times over 10 days; intradermal Freund's adjuvant at 3rd application; 2-week rest; challenge with 0.1 ml topical application; grading at 24 and 48h
evidence.support_text: Na₃ EDTA was tested in a guinea pig repeated insult patch test at 10% concentration. None (0 of 10) of the guinea pigs showed a positive sensitization response, indicating a negative outcome.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig sensitisation test (scoring erythema and swelling)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig (Cavia porcellus), back skin application, scoring at 24 h and 48 h post-application
evidence.support_text: Overall, there was no evidence of significant skin reaction in the... 'primer-coated PMMA' groups (mean scores: 0.2, 0 and 0.2, respectively)...

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig sensitization and elicitation (patch test)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs; i.d. injections of PDC-liposomes (1 mg PDC total in 6 injections, or 0.1 mg PDC per injection, 3 injections per week for 3 weeks); elicitation patch test 3 weeks after last injection.
evidence.support_text: Naive guinea pigs received i.d. PDC-liposomes (1 mg PDC total) in 6 injections. Three weeks later PDC elicitation patch tests showed an irritant contact dermatitis in 5 of 7 guinea pigs, with only 2 showing evidence of sensitization. In a repeated-dose experiment, i.d. PDC-liposomes given as multiple injections resulted in only 1 out of 10 animals showing a positive patch at 6.25 µg PDC, and the other 9 only at irritant 12.5 µg. Therefore, PDC-liposomes given i.d. do not produce an allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig sensitization induction (intradermal) + epicutaneous challenge
evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: intradermal injection of 0.1 ml of 0.01 M beryllium citrate (26.3 µg Be/kg) in guinea pigs, injection site left in situ. Challenge: 15 days later, skin test with 0.1 ml of 0.01 M BeF₂ in MCWT.
evidence.support_text: Table VII, group 5 shows that guinea pigs pretreated with an intradermal injection of beryllium citrate (26.3 µg Be/kg) at a site left in situ, then skin-tested with 0.01 M BeF₂, gave 91% responders (mean score 2.9), demonstrating that beryllium citrate induces skin sensitization to beryllium.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20 guinea pigs (10 test, 10 control); undiluted test substance applied dermally during induction phases I, II, III; trigger concentration test on 3 guinea pigs; observations at 30 and 54 h post-application; vehicle control used
evidence.support_text: Hüls AG (1996e) reported results of the skin sensitization potential of Glyceryl Citrate/Lactate/Linoleate/Oleate using 20 guinea pigs. After induction phases I, II, and III with undiluted test substance and subsequent trigger and patch tests, the study concluded that Glyceryl Citrate/Lactate/Linoleate/Oleate did not induce sensitization in guinea pigs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, challenge concentration >10%.
evidence.support_text: Lamson et al. reported that D&C Yellow no. 11 elicited skin sensitization in guinea pigs at more than 10% challenge concentration.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, cutaneous treatment with 0.1 ml JP-8 four times in a 10-day period before challenge.
evidence.support_text: JP-8 was classified as a weak skin sensitizer based on studies where guinea pigs were cutaneously treated with 0.1 ml JP-8 four times in a 10-day period before the challenge (Kinkead et al., 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction period of at least 2 weeks; challenge on flanks; skin response (redness/edema) recorded at 24 and 48 hr.
evidence.support_text: Styrene oxide was positive in 8 of 10 animals in the guinea pig sensitization tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction period of at least 2 weeks; challenge on flanks; skin response (redness/edema) recorded at 24 and 48 hr.
evidence.support_text: The guinea pig sensitization tests were positive in all 10 animals for p-chlorophenylglycidyl ether.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Intracutaneous injections three times per week for 10 exposures; first induction 0.05 ml, next nine 0.1 ml; challenge 0.05 ml after 2 weeks; scoring 24 h after each injection; guinea pig (Cavia porcellus)
evidence.support_text: Inolex (1975) used two guinea pigs to evaluate the effects of a 0.1% suspension of PEG-2 Stearate. Intracutaneous injections were made three times per week for a total of 10 exposures. After 2 weeks, a challenge injection of 0.05 ml was made. The exposure sites were scored 24 h after each injection. The average score for the 10 sensitizing injections was compared with the score for the challenge. PEG-2 Stearate was considered to be a nonsensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 0.5 M DMA in absorbent ointment, applied to flank, 48 h exposure, 3 times/week for 2 weeks; 2-week rest; Challenge: 0.5 M DMA, 48 h. Species: Hartley white female guinea pig, n=6.
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig sensitization test, 0.5 M DMA in an absorbent ointment was applied to the flank of Hartley white female guinea pigs (n=6) for 48 hours, repeated 3 times per week for 2 weeks. After a 2-week rest period, a 48-hour challenge with 0.5 M DMA resulted in a 100% positive sensitization rate.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig sensitization test (challenge reaction scoring)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs; dermal application of drug-loaded transdermal patch; challenge reaction scored 24 hours after application; n=20
evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig sensitization test, the drug-loaded transdermal patch (the treated group, n=20) showed a sensitization rate of 0% (0/20), a sensitization grade of I, a sensitization classification of 'Weak', and a reaction of 'No', indicating no skin sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: dental filling with zinc-containing amalgam (Septalloy Non Gamma 2 – NG70); patient had prior amalgam fillings; subsequent dermatitis episode lasting 1 week
evidence.support_text: A 45-year-old woman with a history of amalgam fillings received a 9th zinc-containing amalgam filling (Septalloy Non Gamma 2 – NG70: Ag 70%, Sn 18.5%, Cu 11%, Zn 0.5%; mixed with mercury at 1:1.2). Subsequently, she experienced a 1-week episode of facial buccal dermatitis that resolved spontaneously.

evidence.experimental_conditions: epicutaneous patch test on patients with metal-metal hip prostheses; standard reading times
evidence.support_text: In the epicutaneous patch test, 4 out of 16 patients showed an allergic reaction to nickel.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Worker handled Ni NPs without using local exhaust ventilation system, glove box, or respiratory mask.
evidence.support_text: A recent case report described a worker who developed contact dermatitis after handling nickel nanoparticles (Ni NPs) without using a local exhaust ventilation system, glove box, or respiratory mask, indicating that Ni NPs can cause skin sensitization in humans.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Inhalation exposure to nickel nanoparticles in workplace; subsequent elicitation upon contact with bulk nickel in earrings and belt buckles.
evidence.support_text: A chemist who accidentally inhaled NiNP in the workplace subsequently developed symptoms indicative of T-cell-mediated allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) in response to non-nanoparticulate forms of nickel, indicating that NiNP exposure induced skin sensitization as an adverse outcome.

evidence.experimental_conditions: closed patch tests; 48 hours; patients with prosthetic joints; titanium salts
evidence.support_text: None of the patients showed a positive reaction to any of the titanium salts used in the closed patch tests. Two of the four patients patch tested with Metanium ointment produced an eczematous reaction at the test site after 48 hours.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch and intradermal tests; positive defined as papule >5 mm for at least 48 hours; test on chromate-sensitive patients.
evidence.support_text: Table 8 shows that, in contrast to sensitivity to nickel and copper, all but two chromate-sensitive patients showed both positive patch and intradermal tests. A reaction was considered positive when a papule more than 5 mm in diameter was present for at least 48 hours.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch and intradermal tests; tested on eight chromate-sensitive patients.
evidence.support_text: In eight of these patients patch and intradermal tests were done with nickel and copper. None reacted to these metals.
Among 2461 patients with positive patch tests, 546 showed positive patch test results only to nickel (15.73% of females and 6.46% of males), indicating nickel sensitization.

In a dental clinic study (1982-1997), of 311 patients patch tested for dental materials hypersensitivity, 3 patients reacted to copper and cadmium, and 2 patients to copper only. No experimental details were provided.
In the case of our patient we recorded a negative result for nickel, so the theory of concomitant reaction is not possible.

In the case of our patient we recorded a positive reaction to manganese with clinical relevance, as the patient worked with an aluminium alloy containing manganese. A negative result for nickel was also recorded.

One other patient with multiple metal sensitivities appeared to have clinically relevant sensitivity to copper. Presenting with eczema to a golden ring (test to gold negative), the condition resolved when the patient exchanged the gold ring with one made of silver.

evidence.experimental_conditions: brass metal
evidence.support_text: In dermatology patients with hand eczema, patch testing with brass metal gave a positive reaction (Reference /59/).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Clinical patch test with nickel; details not specified
evidence.support_text: We had 4 cases of contact cheilitis caused or aggravated by nickel. The advice given to all 4 patients of using nickel-free cosmetics induced a clinical remission of symptoms, pointing to the relevance of positive patch test responses.

evidence.experimental_conditions: contact with copper metal, reading at 24 h
evidence.support_text: A patient with occupational exposure to copper metal presented with an itching eczematous condition. The individual reacted with necrosis on 24 h testing with copper metal.

evidence.experimental_conditions: copper alloy
evidence.support_text: In a study of 60 dermatology patients with dermatitis, patch testing with copper alloy gave a positive patch reaction (Reference /56/).

evidence.experimental_conditions: copper foil patch
evidence.support_text: Two were positive to copper foil.

evidence.experimental_conditions: copper metal
evidence.support_text: In dermatology patients with hand eczema, patch testing with copper metal gave a positive reaction (Reference /59/).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cutaneous patch testing with metal-salt complexes on the upper back; no specific concentrations or vehicles reported
evidence.support_text: Patch testing of 15 patients with dermatitis after total knee arthroplasty showed that four patients had a 1+ or 2+ reaction to nickel (p. 14).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Day 3 reading (D3)
evidence.support_text: Patch test reactions at D3 revealing contact allergy to cobalt and nickel.

evidence.experimental_conditions: dilute solutions of titanium salts
evidence.support_text: Skin patch testing with dilute solutions of titanium salts gave negative results in all five patients.

evidence.experimental_conditions: dilute titanium salt solutions
evidence.support_text: All five patients patch tested with dilute titanium salt solutions had negative reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: European standard patch test series (TRUEtest, Trolab), reading at 48 and 96 hours
evidence.support_text: We only recorded a positive result for manganese (++/+++, following International Contact Dermatitis Research Group (ICDRG) guidelines); we checked the results after 48 and 96 hr, and it was strongly positive since the first visit. The product we used for patch testing was manganese chloride, at a concentration of 5% in Vaseline, being part of Trolab® metal series.

evidence.experimental_conditions: European Standard series of contact allergens
evidence.support_text: Patch tests using the European Standard series of contact allergens along with cosmetics, emollients and fragrances along with those products used by the patient yielded a positive result only to nickel.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test on 630 females from Danish twin register
evidence.support_text: Bryld et al. patch tested 1076 individuals from the Danish twin register; 146 of 630 females had positive patch test reactions to nickel, indicating allergic sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: human patch test; clinic population 1977-1979; 1499 patients; median age 36 for nickel- and/or cobalt-sensitive women; 72 subjects with nickel sensitivity only
evidence.support_text: In the clinic population from 1977-1979, of those who were only sensitive to nickel, 42 of 72 had or had had hand dermatitis, indicating a positive association.

evidence.experimental_conditions: human patch test; twin study; median age 61; 59 subjects with nickel sensitivity only
evidence.support_text: In the twin study, of 59 subjects with nickel sensitivity only, 18 had or had had hand eczema, indicating a positive association between nickel sensitization and hand eczema.

evidence.experimental_conditions: metallic gold as is (undiluted), part of modified European standard series plus additional chemicals
evidence.support_text: The remainder of the patch tests were negative, including metallic gold as is.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Metallic gold tested as is, reading at D4, tested as part of modified European standard series
evidence.support_text: On patch testing, the remainder of the patch tests were negative, including metallic gold as is.

evidence.experimental_conditions: metallurgy workers, cited from Rudzki et al.

evidence.support_text: In a study by de Groot (1994), members of the Dutch Contact Dermatitis Group and nonmember dermatologists patch tested 1 to 20 patients either suffering from or suspected of suffering from contact allergy to cosmetic products with 30% Hydrogenated Castor Oil in petrolatum. Patch test results indicated no reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 4% in petrolatum, applied to skin of 29 volunteers
evidence.support_text: To evaluate the sensitization potential of 2-ethyl-1-hexanol, a human patch test was conducted on 29 volunteers using 4% 2-ethyl-1-hexanol in petrolatum applied to the skin. The study observed mild inflammation but no sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 48-h occlusive patch, 1% Thymol in petrolatum, tested on patients with eczematous dermatitis.
evidence.support_text: Meneghini et al. (1971) tested 290 patients with eczematous dermatitis using a 48-h occlusive patch with 1% Thymol in petrolatum; no reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% anisyl alcohol in petrolatum; patients with eczema suspected of contact allergy to fragrances or cosmetics (Van Oosten et al., 2009)
evidence.support_text: There were no positive reactions when 5% anisyl alcohol in petrolatum was tested for frequency of contact allergy in a study on patients with eczema suspected of a contact allergy to fragrances or cosmetics (Van Oosten et al., 2009).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% benzyl alcohol in petrolatum; 200 dermatology patients suspected of allergic contact dermatitis
evidence.support_text: When 5% benzyl alcohol in petrolatum was tested in 200 dermatology patients suspected of having allergic contact dermatitis, a positive reaction was elicited in 1%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% benzyl alcohol in petrolatum; 425 Japanese patients with contact dermatitis; study by Nagareda et al., 1992
evidence.support_text: In a study of Japanese patients with contact dermatitis, 3/425 (0.71%) had a positive test reaction to benzyl alcohol, 5% in petrolatum (Nagareda et al., 1992).

review_policy.eligible_subject: unique measurement-producing subject, donor, or cell-system species
